explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/729: for a constant C > 0, are there infinitely many integers a,b,n with a+b > n + C log n such that the denominator of n!/(a!b!) contains only primes ≪_C 1; proved in the affirmative by Barreto and Leeham. The Lean statement: ∀ C > 0, ∃ K ≥ 3, the set of positive triples (a,b,n) with a + b > n + C·log n and no prime p > K dividing the denominator of the rational n!/(a!b!) is infinite. K depends only on C, matching ≪_C 1; 'infinitely many triples' cannot be satisfied degenerately since a prime-bounded denominator bounds a, b in terms of n and K. Stated in the affirmative with the solved/question tags per upstream convention. Faithful.
